entities.name: Jace Beleren
entities.description: A mind mage and planeswalker who follows the journal's trail of cryptoliths to the Drownyard on Innistrad, and blames Liliana for the angels' plight.

entities.name: Liliana Vess
entities.description: A necromancer planeswalker whose voice and image take shape in one of Jace's illusory duplicates, accusing and mocking him; Jace blames her for gathering the angels.

entities.name: Jenrik
entities.description: A colleague of the journal's author, who sent the author a werewolf specimen and spoke of lycanthropy.

entities.name: Lotka
entities.description: A colleague whose predator-prey predictions the journal compares with werewolf fatalities.

entities.name: R. Karolus
entities.description: The rider who delivered the werewolf specimen to the journal's author.

entities.name: Avacyn
entities.description: Innistrad's angel, whose madness the journal links to the cryptoliths.

entities.name: Gideon Jura
entities.description: A planeswalker who taught Jace how to throw a punch.

entities.name: Kiora
entities.description: A planeswalker whom Jace has seen move the entire Halimar Sea.

entities.name: Lavinia
entities.description: An acquaintance of Jace from his time as Guildpact who would have admired his editing eye.

entities.name: Innistrad
entities.description: A plane of endless winter nights where vampires, werewolves, zombies and angels dwell.

entities.name: Gavony
entities.description: A province of Innistrad with moorlands where Jace finds a cryptolith.

entities.name: Nephalia
entities.description: A province of Innistrad with sea cliffs and a reef where cryptoliths all point.

entities.name: Selhoff
entities.description: A port town in Nephalia over the ridge from the cliff path.

entities.name: The Drownyard
entities.description: A massive ring of jagged cryptolith structures jutting from the ocean off Nephalia, the nexus where the cryptoliths point and where angels and zombies gather.

entities.name: Markov Manor
entities.description: The torn-apart manor where Jace found the journal.

entities.name: Kessig
entities.description: A province of Innistrad whose lycanthropes have shown renewed savagery.

entities.name: Ravnica
entities.description: The plane where Jace is Living Guildpact.

entities.name: Zendikar
entities.description: The plane where Jace marched with his companions.

entities.name: Kamigawa
entities.description: The plane of the soratami moonfolk who wrote the journal.

entities.name: Cryptoliths
entities.description: Twisted stones with directional energy fields that warp mana flow and all point toward the Drownyard.

entities.name: The Object
entities.description: A large invisible celestial mass above the Drownyard that the journal says is pulling the tides and moon, appearing to Jace as a blind spot.

entities.name: Jenrik's Journal
entities.description: A dark-leather journal by a soratami scholar recording lunar studies, werewolf dissections and cryptolith findings, which leads Jace to the Drownyard.

entities.name: Soratami
entities.description: The moonfolk of Kamigawa; the journal's author is one, and an illusory duplicate of Jace takes her form.

entities.name: Angels of Innistrad
entities.description: Winged beings who swarm above the Drownyard, drawn by the cryptoliths.

entities.name: Zombies
entities.description: Waterlogged corpses of long-dead sailors who wade in procession through the Drownyard's waters.

entities.name: Werewolves
entities.description: Human-wolf creatures of Innistrad studied in the journal.

events.summary: Jace reaches the Gavony moors in the rain, relieved from the delusions of Markov Manor, and starts reading the journal.
events.quote: It was still evening when he reached Gavony.

events.summary: Journal entry 433: the author dissects a large werewolf specimen sent by Jenrik.
events.quote: With great effort, the rib cage was separated, the specimen split from clavicle to pelvis, its contents exposed to air.

events.summary: The author finds the specimen's interior filled with sinew and almost nothing human, with a large cluster growing on the liver.
events.quote: This one, though. This one was...new.

events.summary: Jace finds a twisted monolith on the moor matching those at Markov Manor and in the journal.
events.quote: The monolith was unmistakably the same as those he had seen at Markov Manor, the same as he had seen in the journal.

events.summary: A spark jumps from the monolith to Jace's hand, and he senses something bright and bell-clear.
events.quote: there was a POP and a spark jumped from the end of the monolith to his hand.

events.summary: Journal entry 643: the cryptoliths warp mana flow, with potentially severe effects on angels.
events.quote: The disruptive properties of the stones appear to also extend to an ability to warp the flow of mana through the region

events.summary: Journal entry 735 traces the stones and tidal distortion to a large reef off the Nephalian coast.
events.quote: a large reef off the coast of Nephalia

events.summary: On the Nephalian cliffs a vacant-eyed fisherwoman tells Jace that a 'she' has arrived with feathered ones from the sky.
events.quote: Brought her feathered ones from the sky, tide came up right on with them!

events.summary: Jace bridges minds with the fisherwoman and finds himself trapped in a featureless dome inside her mind.
events.quote: His form was somehow trapped in someone else's mind.

events.summary: A blind spot at the dome's center swells into a huge Object, and illusory duplicates of Jace appear around him.
events.quote: The blind spot in his vision had swelled to become an Object far larger than Jace himself

events.summary: The dome shatters, revealing a latticed wall of eyes; Jace awakens on the path while the fisherwoman flees.
events.quote: His eyes snapped open to find his hands clapped over his head, his body curled up on the ground.

events.summary: Jace sees the Drownyard, a huge ring of jagged stones in the ocean, and realizes all the cryptoliths point to it.
events.quote: All the cryptoliths point here!

events.summary: The journal proposes that an eldritch moon of great mass is nearing Innistrad.
events.quote: an eldritch moon of sufficient size as to provide a gravitational pull

events.summary: A procession of zombie sailors wades through the shoulder-deep water around the ring.
events.quote: a long procession of shambling humanoids waded through the frigid, shoulder-deep ocean water below.

events.summary: Jace is zapped by a stone again and perceives the Object hovering above the circle, the nexus of Innistrad's redirected leylines.
events.quote: A blind spot, the Object, loomed in his vision, hovering just above the circle of stones in the distance.

events.summary: One of Jace's duplicates takes the form of the soratami author of the journal and recites its words.
events.quote: The pale duplicate had reformed completely into a soratami—one of the moonfolk of Kamigawa.

events.summary: A swarm of angels descends over the Drownyard, dropping feathers.
events.quote: Huge winged things. Angels.

events.summary: The hooded duplicate walks into the sea and drowns, muttering questions.
events.quote: It continued moving doggedly forward as the waters closed over its head, entombing it below the surface.

events.summary: The violet-eyed duplicate reshapes itself into Liliana Vess.
events.quote: slowly it rearranged itself to a familiar form: Liliana Vess.

events.summary: Jace accuses Liliana of redirecting the stones to herd and twist the angels, and she mocks him before vanishing.
events.quote: You're the one who redirected the stones to herd the angels here and twist their minds!

events.summary: The Liliana illusion dissipates into the night air.
events.quote: it suddenly dissipated into the cold night air.

events.summary: The Object disappears from above the ring.
events.quote: The Object had disappeared.

events.summary: A dull buzzing voice tells Jace to stop asking questions and put away the journal, and he decides what he has to do.
events.quote: You don't need the book and its bottomless well of mysteries.

relations.note: He recalls her warning to go home and comes to suspect her of orchestrating events.
relations.quote: This is a dead end. Go home, Jace!

relations.note: Jace's illusory Liliana scorns them as vermin.
All the cryptoliths point toward it.
A port town at the end of Nephalia's road.
relations.quote: The road to Nephalia ended at the base of its sea cliffs, and he could see the roofs of the port town of Selhoff just over the ridge.

relations.note: Gideon taught Jace how to make a fist.
relations.quote: as Gideon had patiently insisted to him
